paper: Pan, Guan, Duan, Feng and Zhou, 'Fixed-Length Dense Fingerprint Representation with Alignment and Robust Enhancement', IEEE TIFS vol. 21 (2026) pp. 1751-1765
display_name: FLARE FDD D=6 / Dual-Pose × Dual-Enhancement / Max Overlap-Masked Cosine

route.statement: a 500 ppi query image I_q and a gallery image I_g
FLARE first estimates the 2D pose using two complementary estimators
we first apply pose estimation and alignment, followed by cropping to 512×512 pixels
the aligned images are then enhanced using two pose estimation methods and two enhancement strategies, producing four augmented versions of each image
each enhanced image is downsampled to 256×256 pixels before being input to the Fixed-length Dense Representation Network
which produces dense descriptors f ∈ R^{2D×16×16} and foreground masks S ∈ R^{1×16×16}
the matching score is computed by measuring the cosine similarity between the flattened dense representations, where only the overlapping foreground regions are considered
the final matching score is obtained by taking the maximum over the four matching scores derived from different pose-enhancement combinations

notes: The branch order is not part of the algorithm, because a maximum does not depend on the order of its arguments. The branch count is.
One fingerprint carries four descriptors of 3072 scalars and four masks of 256, not a single representation of 3072.
